patch.summary:
Thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Wrike documents a broader use-case set; Todoist is narrower/specialist.

Comparison thesis: General-purpose vs specialist. Choose Todoist only if your buying job matches “Personal and team task manager with natural-language capture — Free; Pro from ~$6.25/user/” rather than Wrike's shape. Choose Wrike only if your buying job matches “Enterprise/agency work management with proofing, intake and resourcing — Team from $10/use” rather than Todoist's shape. Workflow advantage: Todoist leans shared coverage; Wrike leans work-management, resource-planning. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Wrike documents a broader use-case set; Todoist is narrower/specialist.
- Positioning: Todoist is Personal and team task manager with natural-language capture — Free; Pro from ~$6.25/user/mo annual; Business ~$10.; Wrike is Enterprise/agency work management with proofing, intake and resourcing — Team from $10/user/mo annual..
- Company-size focus: Todoist (micro, small-business, mid-market) vs Wrike (small-business, mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Todoist-leaning — vs Wrike-leaning work-management, resource-planning, team-collaboration-work.
- Researched limits: Todoist — Not a Work OS or portfolio tool; Wrike — Business tier pricing jump.

Limitations — Todoist: Not a Work OS or portfolio tool; Team features mainly on Business; Wrike: Business tier pricing jump; Heavier admin than lightweight tools.

Poor-fit cases: Todoist is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a Work OS or portfolio tool · Wrike is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Business tier pricing jump · Avoid Todoist if you actually need Wrike's motion (Enterprise/agency work management with proofing, intake and resourcing — Team fr)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
